Class SlotSpec

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.SlotSpec
public final class SlotSpec extends Object
A side-neutral, declarative description of one registered-slot group that a MKCContainerPanel projects onto every container the player opens — the "recipe" half of container parity.

Why a recipe, not a built slot

A real MKCSlot is a per-menu object: the player's own InventoryMenu, every chest/furnace they open, and the creative item-picker each carry their own slot instance for the same logical slot. To make a slot appear on all of them from one registration, the panel can't hold a slot — it holds the instructions to build one, applied fresh to each menu (and bound to that menu's player). That is this class: pure data plus a Player -> Storage factory, evaluated identically on the logical server and the client so the appended slots are byte-identical (the sync-safety contract MKCSlotProjection documents).

It is the parity analogue of the per-call parameters on MKCSlots.Builder: storage, layout, and the client reveal predicate, expressed once as reusable data rather than imperatively against a single menu. MKCContainerPanel turns each SlotSpec into both the real slots (every menu, both sides) and the SlotElements that present them (client).

Inline behavior verbs are sugar over the by-address engine path

Gating, quick-move, binding, and mending are armed in THE ONE WINDOW engine by the slot's Address — that is where slot behavior lives, identically for a vanilla slot and a created slot. The inline verbs here (gate, accepts(Predicate), binding, mending, quickMove) do not introduce a second behavior store: they record the consumer's intent on the spec, and MKCContainerPanel.Builder.register() arms the engine by address for every local index in the group — exactly Window.slot(MKCContainerPanel.address( panelId, groupId, i)).set(KEY, value), the same call a consumer could make by hand. The win is purely ergonomic: behavior is declared where the slot group is declared (no separate forgettable arming pass), and the consumer never computes an address or hand-rolls a per-slot loop. The by-address path stays fully usable; inline is sugar, not a replacement.

Storage is a factory, not a bound storage

MKCSlots.Builder.storage takes an already-player-bound Storage because it runs inside a mixin where the player is in scope. A recipe is registered once at init with no player in scope and is applied to many players' menus, so it takes a Function<Player, Storage> — almost always player -> SOME_ATTACHMENT.bind(player). The factory MUST be deterministic and yield the same storage size for a given player on both sides, or the appended slot block desyncs.

Mutable fluent builder, consumed once by MKCContainerPanel.Builder.addSlot(SlotSpec).

  • Method Details

    • at

      public static SlotSpec at(String groupId)
      Begins a slot-group spec. Position is reactive (Movement ④) — the group's slots flow + wrap into the owning panel's width via SlotFlowElement, so a spec declares only WHAT a group is (storage, count, reveal, behavior), never where it sits.
      Parameters:
      groupId - slot-group id, unique within the owning MKCContainerPanel

    • storage

      public SlotSpec storage(Function<net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.Storage> storageFactory)
      Where items live, as a per-player factory. Required. Use a StorageAttachment-bound factory for content persistence: .storage(player -> POCKETS.bind(player)).

    • count

      public SlotSpec count(int count)
      Number of logical slots in this group (default 1). The storage factory MUST produce a storage of exactly this size for every player, or the appended slot block desyncs across sides.

    • revealWhen

      public SlotSpec revealWhen(BooleanSupplier clientReveal)
      Client-side reveal predicate. The group is visible + interactive on the client only while this returns true; the server keeps it syncing regardless (see MKCSlots.Builder.revealWhen). MUST be client-safe. If unset, the group is always visible.

    • label

      public SlotSpec label(String label)
      MK display name for the group's slots, applied through the naming layer like MKCSlots.Builder.label(String): each slot is named "{label} {n}" (1-based) for a multi-slot group, or just "{label}" for a single slot. If unset, the slots fall back to the capitalized group id. Naming is a client-side display concern (the build seam applies it client-guarded).

    • tooltip

      public SlotSpec tooltip(net.minecraft.network.chat.Component text)
      Attaches a hover tooltip to every slot in this group. The library applies it to each SlotElement it builds (the consumer never touches those instances). Fires only over an EMPTY slot — a slot holding an item shows vanilla's item tooltip instead. Chainable.

    • tooltip

      public SlotSpec tooltip(@Nullable Supplier<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> supplier)
      Supplier-driven variant of tooltip(Component).

    • gate

      public SlotSpec gate(SlotGate gate)
      Arms a SlotGate (what every slot in this group accepts / releases / caps) — sugar for Window.slot(addr).set(MKCBehaviorKeys.GATING, gate) on each local index. Default (unset) is SlotGate.OPEN — pure vanilla.

    • accepts

      public SlotSpec accepts(Predicate<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> accept)
      Convenience over gate: a place-only filter. Builds a SlotGate that admits a stack iff accept passes (pickup stays open, stack cap stays vanilla). For a richer policy (pickup rule, stack cap) declare a full SlotGate via gate.

    • binding

      public SlotSpec binding(boolean enabled)
      Enrolls every slot in this group in Curse-of-Binding enforcement (a bound item can't be taken out while alive, survival only; creative bypasses, §0051) — sugar for set(MKCBehaviorKeys.BINDING, ...). Default off.

    • binding

      public SlotSpec binding()
      Equivalent to binding(true).

    • mending

      public SlotSpec mending(boolean enabled)
      Opts every slot in this group into the XP-orb Mending repair pool (§0053) — sugar for set(MKCBehaviorKeys.MENDING, ...). Default off.

    • mending

      public SlotSpec mending()
      Equivalent to mending(true).

    • quickMove

      public SlotSpec quickMove(com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.QuickMoveParticipation participation)
      Sets how every slot in this group participates in shift-click (quick-move) routing on a foreign menu — sugar for set(MKCBehaviorKeys.QUICK_MOVE, p). Default QuickMoveParticipation.BOTH.
